749986.title: Semgrep findings (8) - static triage
749986.content:
Semgrep (p/default, javascript, typescript, secrets) on repo found 8 findings:

1. `.npmrc:1` MEDIUM - npm-missing-minimum-release-age (no min-release-age set)
2. `components/builder/SiteEditorV2.tsx:313` WARNING - wildcard-postmessage (`postMessage(..., '*')`)
3. `components/builder/SiteEditorV2.tsx:478` WARNING - wildcard-postmessage
4. `components/builder/SiteEditorV2.tsx:492` WARNING - wildcard-postmessage
5. `components/builder/SitePreviewV2.tsx:19` WARNING - react-dangerouslysetinnerhtml (`rendered.css`)
6. `components/builder/SitePreviewV2.tsx:20` WARNING - `rendered.body`
7. `components/builder/SitePreviewV2.tsx:21` WARNING - `rendered.script`
8. `lib/validators/site-onboarding.ts:200` WARNING - detect-non-literal-regexp (RegExp with `domain` arg → potential ReDoS)

Note: The dangerouslySetInnerHTML sinks feed from `renderSiteV2()` which internally applies `escapeHtml`/`safeUrl`/`sanitizeLink` to user content - the XSS posture there was reviewed as mostly escaped by parent. postMessage('*') is in editor iframe; editor posts to parent, low risk on its own but worth a look.

No hardcoded secrets found by gitleaks (no-git) or trufflehog.

4cb813.title: Authorization audit results: model is consistent, no new IDOR/BFLA confirmed
4cb813.content:
Performed a route-by-route authorization (IDOR/BFLA) audit across app/api/sites/*, billing, admin/users, auth/*, ai/*, generate-logo, map-sites, public/*.

## Ownership enforcement (verified)
- Centralized path via `assertSiteAccess`/`siteAccessWhere` (lib/site/access.ts): site [GET/PATCH/PUT/DELETE], template, media, sections/[sectionId]/improve. Non-admin→ `OR [{userId}, {userId:null,guestTokenHash,guestExpiresAt>now}]`; ADMIN bypasses with `{id}`.
- Inline pattern `user.role === "ADMIN" ? {} : { userId: user.id }`: download, publish, leads/export, sections (POST), sections/[sectionId] (PATCH/DELETE with `site:{is:{userId}}`), clone-v2, improve-content, revisions/[revisionId]/restore, domain.
- All these bind site → user correctly; section/revision binds are additionally scoped to their parent siteId, so cross-resource IDOR is prevented.

## BFLA / privilege escalation
- No EDITOR→ADMIN path. Register schema forces default role EDITOR and doesn't accept role; /api/admin/users (POST) requires existing ADMIN session; admin pages verify role server-side (`app/admin/*`).
- Billing webhook is signed (stripe signature), checkout binds client_reference_id to the session user.

## Guest model
- Guest-owned sites (userId:null) only match the correct guestTokenHash; after register/login claimGuestProjects nulls guestTokenHash and sets userId. No cross-user guest takeover confirmed.

## Note on map-sites
- GET /api/map-sites returns businessName + location + id + createdAt for ALL sites with non-null location with NO auth and NO status filter, including DRAFT (unpublished) sites of other users. This is a real broken-collection-level authorization / information disclosure. This finding is assigned to the sibling Map-Sites agent (68f6f6c5); not re-filed here to avoid duplicate.
- Other public endpoints (public leads, cover, view, pexels images/videos, generate-site/generate-logo) are intentionally public onboarding functions with rate limits - not findings.

## Conclusion
Authorization model is disciplined and consistent. No additional exploitable IDOR/BFLA beyond the map-sites collection exposure (owned by sibling). CSRF mitigated by SameSite=Lax on state-changing cookies. Session/password handling is sound (scrypt, httpOnly, random tokens).

9c7544.title: Auth/CSRF/Business-Logic scope conclusions (Auth agent)
9c7544.content:
Assessed authentication, session, CSRF, and business-logic areas of this Next.js codebase. Findings:

1. LOGIN BRUTE-FORCE CONTROL (weak, hardening)
- lib/auth login route uses rate limiting keyed by `${ip}:${username.toLowerCase()}` (5 attempts/15min).
- The IP source is parsed from spider-able `x-forwarded-for` header (first value) with also `x-real-ip` fallback. Both are client/spoofable at the edge unless a trusted proxy overwrites them.
- Because the limit key includes the username, an attacker enumerates user@example.com-style logins by rotating usernames while spoofing per-request X-Forwarded-For, defeating the per-account throttle. No per-account/IP lockout across a distrusted identity.
- Net: weak brute-force protection; does not demonstrate unauthorized data access by itself; treat as hardening observation not a full vulnerability report.

2. CSRF POSTURE
- All state-changing routes (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE under /api/sites, /api/auth/login|logout|register, /api/billing/*) rely on the session cookie `__cluster_session` with `sameSite: "lax"` and no CSRF token.
- SameSite=lax blocks cross-origin POST/PUT/DELETE, so classic cross-site CSRF against these is largely mitigated in modern browsers.
- Gap: no explicit Origin/Referer validation and no CSRF token; defense-in-depth recommendation. Also GET-based info endpoints (map-sites, leads/export, download) are not state-changing, so not CSRF-exposed directly.

3. PASSWORD HASHING
- lib/password.ts uses Node `scrypt` with default parameters (`scrypt(password, salt, 64)` — default N=16384, r=8, p=1) and 16-byte random salt. Acceptable but below current OWASP guidance (N=2^17). Minor crypto hardening note.

4. PASSWORD RESET FLOW (adequate)
- randomBytes(32) token, stored hashed (sha256 hashToken), 30-min expiry, single-use via usedAt, revokes all sessions on completion. Registration rate-limited 3/hr. No enumeration (always returns ok). Solid.

5. ADMIN ESCALATION (no bypass found)
- Register defaults to EDITOR (zod schema), role not user-controllable.
- /api/admin/users requires existing ADMIN session (role check) → 403 for editors.
- Admin bootstrap via scripts/create-admin.mjs requires env ADMIN_PASSWORD (min 10 chars) — no default credentials in repo.
- Guest→owned project transfer (claimGuestProjects) requires matching guestTokenHash + not-expired; low risk.

6. BILLING WEBHOOK LOGIC (reasonable)
- checkout.session.completed reads `session.client_reference_id` (server-set = user.id) to set planStatus ACTIVE. Not attacker-controllable since event is signature-verified via Stripe webhook secret.
- Idempotency via unique RateLimit key `stripe-event:${id}`; duplicate → 200 duplicate. Race handled.
- hasProAccess = ADMIN or planStatus ACTIVE; consistent across download/publish/domain/media quotas.
- No self-service privilege self-promotion found; no ability to set planStatus without Stripe webhook.

7. OPEN REDIRECT in checkout `from` param — NOT exploitable
- Server validates `from` requiring startsWith("/") and not startsWith("//"); client (billing page) re-validates with same rule before embedding. No protocol-relative `//evil.com` allowed. Not a deliverable open redirect.

CONCLUSION: No high-severity, PoC-backed auth/CSRF/business-logic vulnerability found in this scope. Several hardening observations (weak login rate-limit key, default scrypt cost, missing CSRF tokens/Origin checks). Filed none as full vulnerability reports because none demonstrates an unauthorized confidentiality/integrity/availability impact that meets the reporting gate.

dd1baa.title: XSS render-layer conclusion (v2 + legacy)
dd1baa.content:
XSS posture review of the rendering paths:

lib/site/v2-render.ts consistently escapes all user-controlled text via the local `escapeHtml` helper (business name, section titles/subtitles/body, CTA labels, list items, SEO title/description, meta og/twitter fields) and sanitizes every URL via `safeUrl`/`sanitizeLink` (allows only https:, /, #, mailto:, tel:; rejects http://, javascript:, data:, vbscript:). Theme colors are validated against known tokens or hex regex. The generated `<style>`/`<script>` for editor mode and the form/nav/gallery scripts are fully static strings with no user interpolation. LD+JSON uses JSON.stringify(...).replace(/</g, "\\u003c"). No reachable XSS sink confirmed in the V2 pipeline.

Legacy V1 path (components/builder/SitePreview.tsx + lib/site/section-composer.ts + export-html.ts): reviewed and no raw dangerouslySetInnerHTML with unescaped user content was confirmed as a stored-XSS trigger within the auditing budget; the V1 editor preview and public pages render through typed React components.

Overall: no confirmed, PoC-backed stored/reflected XSS. The escaping in v2-render is complete. Recommendation (defense-in-depth): add a Content-Security-Policy header in next.config.mjs and validate that legacy V1 SitePreview escapes any free-form text similarly.
